messages.subject: how to work with paired frequencies in a corpus
messages.subject_clean: how to work with paired frequencies in a corpus
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

 

I am in the process of doing a corpus study on written Maltese,
and we are interested in the frequency of spelling variants.

 

We generated a file of paired spellings (a canonical and a "facebook" one,
if you will).

In the absence of a full electronic dictionary of Maltese words (there is
one, but it has many gaps),

we simply looked for tokens in the corpus and then made pairs of variants
that occurred at least once in the corpus.

So, for each pair, we have at least one example of a canonical and one of a
"facebook" spelling.

 

We are now interested in whether there is a relation between the overall
frequency of a word

and the likelihood that the "facebook" spelling is preferred.

(similar to the effect that high-frequency words are more likely to be
spoken in a reduced form)

 

I did an analysis on the log of the proportion of both frequencies,

and found a relation of the likelihood of the "facebook" spelling to the
overall frequency.

But then I realized that the relation may be an artefact.

 

Because there is by definition (given how we generated the data set) at
least one example of each spelling,

the potential maximal proportion of the "facebook" spelling is related to
the overall frequency:

For words with an overall frequency of 2, the ratio of the spellings is
necessarily 1/1 (because the overall frequency of 2 means
that there is one example of each variant), for an overall frequency of 3
the maximal ratio is 2/1, for 4 it is 3 over 1 and so on.

 

How can I now test a relation between the likelihood of the alternative
spelling that accounts for that?

That is, can how can I correct the log ratio to account for the fact that
there is a relation between the overall frequency
and the maximal possible (log) ratio?

 

Kind regards,

Holger
